source: Electric motor hardware and motor layouts (owner 2026-10-21: 'add options for single, dual, tri and quad-motor and add different motors with different weight. Base the motor specs loosely on real electric motors on the market'). A drive unit is the whole package a car buys: motor, inverter and the unit's own fixed reduction gear, so mass_kg covers all three and reduction_ratio is the ratio of that gear. Every number is [AS]: a loose, rounded class figure after the published numbers named in each unit's 'source', never a measured or claimed OEM datasheet, and the inspirations are class names only. The shipped car_electric motor (600 N*m, 300 kW, 20000 rpm, 80 kg, 9:1) is the car's own 'stock' unit and is not listed here. regen_torque_nm is a light fraction of the peak torque [AS] (the shipped motor regenerates at one sixth of its peak); efficiency is the motor-and-inverter figure on the same simple scale physics_sim's electric_motor uses. reduction_efficiency is the mesh efficiency of the unit's gear (physics_sim differential or gear_pair 'efficiency'). The layout of the motors is a generic transform of the vehicle file's powertrain (rg/ev_motor.h), never a per-car file: an axle unit is motor -> open differential -> two hubs, a per-wheel unit is motor -> gear_pair (the reduction) -> one hub.

layouts.name: Single motor
layouts.description: One drive unit on the rear axle, through an open differential. Lightest and cheapest: the front axle is not driven (rear-wheel drive).

layouts.name: Dual motor
layouts.description: One drive unit per axle, each through an open differential (all-wheel drive). The two units get the same torque command: there is no torque vectoring between them.

layouts.name: Tri motor
layouts.description: One drive unit on the front axle and one motor on each rear wheel (three motors, all-wheel drive). Every motor gets the same torque command: there is no torque vectoring, and the rear wheels have no differential.

layouts.name: Quad motor
layouts.description: One motor on every wheel (four motors, all-wheel drive, no differentials). Every motor gets the same torque command: there is no torque vectoring. Each motor carries its unit's full figures, so power and weight grow with the motor count.

units.label: Economy PMSM
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of a 110 kW / 320 N*m, 10400 rpm permanent-magnet synchronous front unit with a single-stage reduction of about 8:1; mass of motor, inverter and reduction rounded from typical 120-130 kg drive units. Not an OEM datasheet.

units.label: Compact induction
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of a small AC induction drive unit (about 150 kW, 330 N*m, 16000 rpm, 9:1 single-stage reduction); light because it needs no magnets, lower efficiency than a permanent-magnet machine. Not an OEM datasheet.

units.label: Compact PMSM
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of a rear permanent-magnet drive unit of about 210 kW and 420 N*m at up to 18000 rpm with a 9:1 reduction; mass of motor, inverter and gearbox rounded from the typical 80-90 kg of such a unit. Not an OEM datasheet.

units.label: Axial flux
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of a 790 N*m, 200 kW peak axial-flux machine of about 37 kg that turns only 7000 rpm, so its own reduction is a low 4:1 (unit mass here adds an assumed inverter and gear to the bare machine). Not an OEM datasheet.

units.label: High-density PMSM
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of a very compact, high-speed (about 20000 rpm) permanent-magnet drive unit near 380 kW and 640 N*m for about 75 kg including its inverter and gear. Not an OEM datasheet.

units.label: Hypercar unit
units.source: [AS] after the published class figures of an oil-cooled hypercar per-wheel drive unit (about 450 kW and 650 N*m, 15000 rpm, a short reduction for a top speed beyond 300 km/h) with a strong regeneration limit; mass of motor, inverter and reduction rounded. Not an OEM datasheet.
